an3.128:3.1: “Here, mendicants, in the morning I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Varanasi for alms.
an3.128:3.2: While I was walking for alms near the cow-hitching place at the wavy leaf fig, mendicants, I saw a disgruntled monk who was looking for pleasure in external things, unmindful, without situational awareness or immersion, with straying mind and undisciplined faculties.
an3.128:4.2: If you’re bitter, festering with putrefaction, flies will, without a doubt, plague and infest you. This is not the case.’
an3.128:4.3: So, mendicants, that monk was struck with a sense of urgency by this advice of mine”.
